transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. I'm here because... well, I'm actually on administrative leave from my job right now. I work in HR. Which, honestly, is usually just endless red tape. Like, we’ve been trying to replace the coffee machines in the breakrooms for six months, and the facilities manager keeps insisting we do a 'pilot program' for a new espresso maker. A pilot program for coffee! It’s ridiculous. He’s the kind of guy who color-codes his inbox and drives exactly the speed limit, you know? Just zero sense of urgency. 

But anyway... I couldn't deal with the waiting anymore on my end for this other project, so I just pushed ahead with our new onboarding launch. I went ahead and committed company money and booked a lot of vendor time before any of the official approvals were actually in place. 

At the time, it felt so bold. It felt completely necessary, like someone finally had to just take charge and make things happen. But now... yeah, now they've put me on leave, and everyone at the office is asking what I was thinking.
In the time leading up to when you made that decision at work, did you feel unusually energetic or like you didn’t need as much sleep?

Sleep... you know, I haven't really thought about it. I mean, maybe? I was just so focused on getting the onboarding thing off the ground. It's funny you mention sleep, actually, because my neighbor just bought this enormous wind chime. Like, industrial sized. Who needs a wind chime that big? It sounds like a cathedral every time there's a breeze, which is constantly because we live right at the top of this hill. I've been meaning to go over there and say something, but he's got this massive dog that always looks like it's plotting my demise. A Rottweiler mix, I think. Beautiful coat, though. Really shiny. He must feed it raw eggs or something. But yeah, energy-wise... I don't know, I just felt like I was finally getting things done, you know?
Looking back, did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual during that time, or that you felt rested even if you didn’t sleep much?

I honestly couldn't tell you. I wasn't really keeping track of the hours or paying attention to whether I was tired. I was actually spending a lot of time out in the living room anyway because my wife had just bought this new throw rug. It's one of those supposedly authentic Moroccan ones, you know? Hand-woven, really intricate geometric pattern. 

But the thing sheds everywhere. I swear I'm vacuuming up these little red wool fibers twice a day. We actually went out and bought one of those cordless Dyson vacuums just to keep up with it. The guy at the store swore it was the best model they had, but the battery life is an absolute joke. You leave it plugged in for three hours and get maybe fifteen minutes of actual suction before it dies. It's a total scam. I keep meaning to write an online review about it, maybe warn some people before they drop that kind of money. 

But yeah, sleep... I really don't know. I just wasn't paying attention to it at the time.
During that time when you were pushing forward with the onboarding project, did you notice your mood being unusually high, elated, or irritable—like you were on edge or easily annoyed?

Well, yeah, actually. For the past few weeks before they put me on leave, I just felt... brilliantly alive. Like I was finally the one who was going to show leadership what HR can actually be, you know? We aren't just paper pushers. But then, if someone pushed back on me, I would get suddenly furious. Like, instantly enraged over the most minor things, like small edits to a slide deck or routine budget questions. 

Which reminds me, the guy in finance who handles our budgets, Greg? He just got one of those standing desks. Have you seen those? He’s got the whole setup with the ergonomic anti-fatigue mat and everything, and he just stands there all day looking like he’s commanding a starship. My brother-in-law actually tried one of those treadmill desks a couple of years ago, but he ended up spilling hot coffee all over his laptop because he tripped while he was trying to walk and talk on a Zoom call at the same time. It was a complete disaster. He had to pay out of pocket to replace the motherboard because AppleCare didn't cover liquid damage. AppleCare is such a racket anyway, you read the fine print and they basically cover nothing. It's like paying for air. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, I felt amazing, but if anyone questioned my project or my budget, I just completely lost it on them.
During the time when you felt so energized and focused on the project, did you find yourself moving around more, feeling restless, or having trouble staying still?

Oh, absolutely. Sitting at my desk felt almost impossible. It was like my body had a literal motor in it. I was getting to the office way before anyone else, just walking the floors, constantly rewriting my presentation decks, firing off emails, completely rearranging our project plans... just constantly in motion. 

Speaking of motors, though, my neighbor—not the one with the wind chime, the guy on the other side—he's been restoring this 1969 Mustang in his driveway. And I mean, it's a beautiful car, classic cherry red, but he revs the engine at the most absurd hours. Like, 6:30 AM on a Sunday. And he uses this specific chemical engine degreaser that smells exactly like black licorice. I absolutely hate black licorice. When I was a kid, my grandmother used to keep a glass bowl of those Good & Plenty candies on her coffee table, and they were always totally stale. You'd bite into one and it was like chewing on a piece of chalk. She had this weird obsession with keeping everything in little glass bowls, actually. Decorative soaps, potpourri, mixed nuts... it was a whole aesthetic she had going on in the nineties. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the restlessness. Yeah, I just couldn't stay in my chair. I was just pacing the office and emailing people non-stop.
Looking back, did you feel like you could function well on very little sleep, or that you didn’t need to sleep as much as usual during that time?

I mean, I think you already asked me about sleep, right? Like I said, I really couldn't tell you. I wasn't paying attention to the clock or how many hours I was getting. I was just... doing things. 

Like I mentioned, I was spending a lot of time in the living room anyway. That rug really is a nightmare, though. My wife is talking about maybe taking it back, but I don't even know if you can return a rug once it's been walked on for a month. We'd probably have to rent one of those industrial steam cleaners from the hardware store just to make it look new again. Have you ever rented one of those? They are so heavy. I helped a buddy move a few years ago and we rented one to clean his old apartment before the walk-through, and getting that thing up three flights of stairs almost killed my lower back. I had to go to a chiropractor for like six weeks after that. He was this guy who insisted on playing Enya softly in the background during the adjustments. It was incredibly weird. 

But yeah, the sleep thing... I don't know. I just wasn't focused on it.

We had a golden retriever when I was a kid, actually, named Buster. He was a great dog, but he had this terrible habit of eating our socks. My mom was always furious because she'd buy these expensive wool socks for the winter, and Buster would just swallow them whole. We had to take him to the vet twice to get them surgically removed. The vet was this really tall guy, Dr. Henderson, who always wore these brightly colored bow ties. It was kind of his signature look. I think he thought it made him look less intimidating to the animals, but honestly, if I were a dog, a guy in a neon green polka-dot bow tie coming at me with a thermometer would terrify me. 

But anyway... what did you ask me? Sleep? Yeah, I don't know. I just wasn't keeping track of it.

It's like when you're on a long road trip, you know? You don't sit there staring at the odometer the whole time. You just drive. I drove cross-country once right after college. Me and my buddy Dave, in this beat-up Honda Civic that didn't have working AC. We drove all the way from Chicago to Seattle in July. It was brutal. We survived entirely on beef jerky and those giant fountain sodas from gas stations. We stopped at this one place in South Dakota, near the Badlands, and they had this giant concrete dinosaur out front. Like, fifty feet tall, painted bright green. Dave insisted on climbing it to take a picture, and he ended up ripping his favorite pair of cargo shorts right down the seam. He had to tie a flannel shirt around his waist for the next three days until we found a Target. Cargo shorts were huge back then, though. Everyone had them. The more pockets, the better. I used to carry my Discman in one pocket, my keys in another, a wallet on a chain... 

Look, I'm sorry, I'm getting frustrated because I feel like we're going in circles. I don't know how much I slept. I just didn't need to. I was fine. Can we talk about something else?
